semin-durr:1-1.t:
His saying: {أُوحِيَ}: This is the reading of the majority, I mean from «أَوْحَى», the quadriliteral form. al-ʿAtakī on the authority of Abū ʿAmr, Ibn Abī ʿAbla and Abū Iyās read «وُحِيَ», the triliteral; the two are dialectal forms, and one says «وحى إليه كذا» and «أَوْحاه إليه» with one meaning. A verse of al-ʿAjjāj was recited:
4346 - وَحَى لها القرارَ فاسْتَقَرَّت
(He revealed to it its settling place, and it settled.) Zayd ibn ʿAlī, al-Kisāʾī in one transmission, and Ibn Abī ʿAbla also read «أُحِي» with a hamza with ḍamma and no wāw after it. This was explained as the hamza being a substitute for the wāw with ḍamma, as in «أُعِدَ» for «وُعِدَ»; so this is a branch of the reading «وُحِيَ» in the triliteral. al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is of the unrestricted substitution (qalb), whose permissibility applies to every wāw with ḍamma, and al-Māzinī even made it unrestricted for the wāw with kasra as well, as in إشاح and إسادة and {إعَآءِ أَخِيهِ} [Yūsuf: 76]." The Shaykh said: "It is not as he stated; rather, there is a breakdown in this: the wāw with ḍamma may be initial, medial or final, and each has its rules; and in some of that there is disagreement and a detailed treatment mentioned in grammar." I say: this has already been discussed fully at the start of this work, and praise belongs to Allah. Then the Shaykh said, after relating from him what I gave above from al-Māzinī: "This is multiplying (of examples) and boasting. He used to mention that in Sūrat Yūsuf at His saying {وِعَآءِ أَخِيهِ} [Yūsuf: 76]. From al-Māzinī there are two statements on this: one, analogy as he stated; the other, restricting that to what is heard." I say: the scholars have not ceased mentioning a parallel together with its parallel; and when he mentioned the substitution of the hamza, which is regular according to all, he mentioned its substitution where there is disagreement.
His saying: {أَنَّهُ استمع}: This is what stands in the place of the agent, because it is the explicit direct object; and according to the Kufans and al-Akhfash it is permissible that the preposition and its genitive noun stand in its place, so this remains in the accusative. The implied form is: "It was revealed to me that a group listened." «مِنْ الجنِّ» is an adjective of «نَفَرٌ». The describing of the Qur'an as "wondrous" (عَجَب) is either by way of intensification, or with an omitted muḍāf (first term), that is: "possessing wonder", or in the sense of the active participle, that is, "wonder-inspiring" (مُعْجِب). «يَهْدِي» is another adjective.

semin-durr:2-2.t: The majority read {الرشد} with ḍamma and sukūn; Ibn ʿUmar read it with two ḍammas, and from him also with two fatḥas. This was discussed in al-Aʿrāf.

semin-durr:3-3.t:
His saying: {وَأَنَّهُ تعالى جَدُّ رَبِّنَا}: "The two brothers" (al-akhawān) [Translator's note: i.e. Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī], Ibn ʿĀmir and Ḥafṣ read «أنَّ» with fatḥa, and what is conjoined to it with wāw, in twelve words; the rest read it with kasra. Ibn ʿĀmir and Abū Bakr read «وإنه لَمَّا قام» with kasra, and the rest with fatḥa; they agreed on fatḥa in His saying: {وَأَنَّ المساجد لِلَّهِ}. The summary of this: the doubled «أنَّ» in this sūra is of three kinds. A kind that does not have the conjunctive wāw with it: there is no disagreement among the readers about its fatḥa or kasra, according to how the recitation came and what Arabic requires, as in His saying: {قُلْ أُوحِيَ إِلَيَّ أَنَّهُ استمع}, where there is no disagreement about its fatḥa because it stands in the place of the maṣdar, and as in His saying: {إِنَّا سَمِعْنَا قُرْآناً} [al-Jinn: 1], where there is no disagreement about its kasra because it is quoted after «قال».
The second kind is that it is joined to the wāw, and these are fourteen words. One of them, on which there is no disagreement about its fatḥa, is His saying, the Exalted: {وَأَنَّ المساجد لِلَّهِ} [al-Jinn: 18], and this is the third kind. The second is: {وَأَنَّهُ لَّمَا قَامَ} [al-Jinn: 19], which Ibn ʿĀmir and Abū Bakr read with kasra and the rest with fatḥa. The remaining twelve were read with fatḥa by the two brothers, Ibn ʿĀmir and Ḥafṣ, and with kasra by the rest, as the whole matter was set out earlier. The twelve are His saying: {وَأَنَّهُ تعالى جَدُّ رَبِّنَا}, {وَأَنَّهُ كَانَ يَقُولُ} [al-Jinn: 4], {وَأَنَّا ظَنَنَّآ} [al-Jinn: 5], {وَأَنَّهُ كَانَ رِجَالٌ} [al-Jinn: 6], {وَأَنَّهُمْ ظَنُّواْ} [al-Jinn: 7], {وَأَنَّا لَمَسْنَا} [al-Jinn: 8], {وَأَنَّا كُنَّا} [al-Jinn: 9], {وَأَنَّا لاَ ندري} [al-Jinn: 10], {وَأَنَّا مِنَّا الصالحون} [al-Jinn: 11], {وَأَنَّا ظَنَنَّآ} [al-Jinn: 12], {وَأَنَّا لَمَّا سَمِعْنَا} [al-Jinn: 13], {وَأَنَّا مِنَّا المسلمون} [al-Jinn: 14]. When you know their arrangement from the standpoint of the readings, turn to the explanation of that.
People differed about this. Abū Ḥātim said about the fatḥa: "It is conjoined to the nominative of «أُوْحِيَ», so all of them are in the position of the nominative for what is not named its agent (nāʾib fāʿil)." What he said has been rejected by people, because most of them cannot be included under what «أُوْحِي» governs. Do you not see that if it were said: "It was revealed to me that we touched the sky, and that we were, and that we do not know, and that among us are the righteous, and that when we heard, and that among us are the Muslims," its meaning would not be coherent? Makkī said: "The conjunction of «أنَّ» with { آمَنَّا بِهِ} [al-Jinn: 2] is more complete in meaning than conjunction with «أنَّه استمعَ», because if you conjoined {وَأَنَّا ظَنَنَّآ} [al-Jinn: 5], {وَأَنَّا لَمَّا سَمِعْنَا} [al-Jinn: 13], {وَأَنَّهُ كَانَ رِجَالٌ مِّنَ الإنس} [al-Jinn: 6], {وَأَنَّا لَمَسْنَا} [al-Jinn: 8] and the like to {أَنَّهُ استمع} [al-Jinn: 1], it would not be allowed, because it is not among what was revealed to him; it is only a command or a report, and it is about themselves. The kasra is clearer in this, and a group of readers hold it."
The second: that the fatḥa in those is a conjunction on the position of «به» in «آمَنَّا به». al-Zamakhsharī said: "As though he had said: we believed in it, and we believed that He, the Exalted, is the majesty of our Lord, and that our fool used to say, and likewise the rest." Makkī, however, weakened this view and said: "The fatḥa in these is by carrying over the meaning of «آمَنَّا به», and there is remoteness in the meaning, because they did not report that they believed it when they heard the guidance, and they did not report that they believed that there were men; Allah only related that they said this, reporting about themselves to their companions, so kasra is preferable for this." What he said is not necessary, for the meaning on that basis is sound.
al-Farrāʾ and al-Zajjāj preceded al-Zamakhsharī in this analysis. But al-Farrāʾ sensed a difficulty and resolved it; he said: "«أنَّ» was given fatḥa because belief falls upon it, and you find belief fits in some of what has fatḥa and not others, which does not prevent carrying them all through with fatḥa, for something fits in them that necessitates the fatḥa of «أنَّ», such as 'we affirmed' and 'we testified,' as the Arabs said:
4347 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... وزَجَّجْنَ الحواجبَ والعُيونا
(…and they lengthened the eyebrows and the eyes.) so he put «العيونَ» in the accusative by conjoining it to «الحواجب», though eyes are not lengthened (تُزَجَّج); they are lined with kohl, so he supplied the kohl for it." End of quotation. So he pointed to something of what Makkī mentioned and answered it. al-Zajjāj said: "But its explanation is that it be carried over to the meaning of «آمنَّا به», because the meaning of «آمَنَّا به» is 'we affirmed it and we knew it,' so the meaning would be: we affirmed that He, the Exalted, is the majesty of our Lord."
The third: that it is conjoined to the hāʾ in «به», that is: "we believed in it, and that He, the Exalted, is the majesty of our Lord, and that he used to say," to the end. This is the school of the Kufans. Although it is strong in meaning, it is barred on technical grounds, because, as you know, the genitive pronoun is not conjoined to except by repeating the preposition. These two views were investigated fully in Sūrat al-Baqara at His saying: {وَكُفْرٌ بِهِ والمسجد الحرام} [al-Baqara: 217]. Makkī, however, strengthened this view on another ground, which is very good. May Allah have mercy on him; he said: "Conjunction to the genitive pronoun without repeating the preposition in the case of «أنَّ» is better than elsewhere, because the preposition is dropped so frequently with «أنَّ»."
The basis of the kasra is conjunction to His saying: {إِنَّا سَمِعْنَا} [al-Jinn: 1], so all of it is governed by "saying", that is: "so they said: 'we heard,' and they said: 'He, the Exalted, is the majesty of our Lord,'" to the end. Some said: the two clauses {وَأَنَّهُ كَانَ رِجَالٌ} [al-Jinn: 6] and {وَأَنَّهُمْ ظَنُّواْ} [al-Jinn: 7] are parenthetical between the speech of the jinn, and they are from the speech of the Creator, the Exalted; but the apparent view is that they are from their speech, said by some of them to others. The basis of kasra and fatḥa in His saying {وَأَنَّهُ لَّمَا قَامَ عَبْدُ الله} [al-Jinn: 19] is what has gone before. As for the basis of their agreement on the fatḥa of {وَأَنَّ المساجد} [al-Jinn: 18], there are two views. One: that it is conjoined to {أَنَّهُ استمع} [al-Jinn: 1], so it also is revealed. The other: that it is with an omitted preposition, that preposition being attached to the verb of prohibition, that is: "so do not call upon anyone along with Allah, because the mosques belong to Allah." Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned both.
al-Zamakhsharī said: "«أنه استمع» has fatḥa because it is the agent of «أُوْحي», and {إِنَّا سَمِعْنَا} [al-Jinn: 1] has kasra because it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) quoted after "saying." Then the rest are carried over to these two: what was of the revelation is given fatḥa, and what was of the speech of the jinn is given kasra, and all of them are from their speech except the last two, namely {وَأَنَّ المساجد} [al-Jinn: 18] and {وَأَنَّهُ لَّمَا قَامَ عَبْدُ الله} [al-Jinn: 19]. Whoever gave fatḥa to all of them did so by conjunction to the position of the preposition and its genitive noun in {آمَنَّا بِهِ} [al-Jinn: 2], that is: we affirmed it, and we affirmed that He…"
The majority read {جَدُّ رَبِّنَا} with fatḥa, annexed to «رَبِّنا»; what is meant by it here is majesty. It was said: His power and His command. It was said: His remembrance. الجَدّ is also good fortune (ḥaẓẓ), and from this the saying of the Prophet, peace be upon him: "and the fortune of the fortunate is of no avail against You." الجَدّ is also the father of the father, and الجِدّ with kasra is the opposite of slackness in a matter.
ʿIkrima read it with ḍamma on the bāʾ of «رَبُّنا» and tanwīn on «جَدٌّ», making «ربُّنا» a badal (substitute) for «جَدٌّ», الجَدّ meaning "great", as though it were said: "and He, the Exalted, is great, our Lord," so a definite word is substituted for an indefinite one. From him also: «جَدَّاً» accusative with tanwīn and «رَبُّنا» nominative. The explanation is that «جَدَّاً» is accusative as tamyīz (specification), and «ربُّنا» is the agent of «تعالى», which was transferred from agency, since the implied form is: "the majesty of our Lord was exalted," then "our Lord was exalted" became "majesty", that is, greatness, like «تَصَبَّبَ زيدٌ عَرَقاً», meaning "the sweat of Zayd poured." From him also, and from Qatāda likewise, but with kasra on the jīm, and there are two views on it. One: that it is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, and «ربُّنا» is the agent of «تعالى», the implied form being: "our Lord was exalted with an earnest exaltation," that is, in truth and not falsehood. The other: that it is accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial), that is: "our Lord was exalted in truth and firmly"; Ibn ʿAṭiyya said this.
Ḥumayd ibn Qays read «جُدُّ ربِّنا» with ḍamma on the jīm, annexed to «ربِّنا»; it has the sense of "great", as Sībawayh related. Originally it is the annexation of an adjective to the noun it describes, since the original is "our great Lord", like «جَرْدُ قَطِيفة», whose original is «قطيفة جَرْدٌ» ("a worn-out velvet cloth"); it is interpreted so by the Basrans. Ibn al-Samayfaʿ read «جَدَى رَبِّنا» with an alif after the dāl, annexed to «ربِّنا». الجَدى and الجَدْوى mean benefit and gift, that is: "the gift of our Lord and His benefit was exalted."
The hāʾ in «أنَّه استمعَ», «وأنَّه تعالى» and what comes after is the pronoun of the affair and the matter (ḍamīr al-amr wa-l-shaʾn), and what follows it is the khabar of «أنَّ». His saying {مَا اتخذ صَاحِبَةً} is a fresh sentence containing an affirmation of the exaltation of His majesty.

semin-durr:4-4.t: His saying: {سَفِيهُنَا}: It may be the ism (subject) of kāna, with «يقول» as the khabar (predicate). Had a clause like this not stood as the khabar of «كان», placing it first would be impossible: if you said «يقولُ سفيهُنا» by inversion, rather than «سفيهُنا يقول», it would not be allowed. The difference is that outside the chapter of kāna it is confused with verb and agent, whereas in the chapter of kāna that is not feared. The second view: that «سفيهُنا» is the agent of «يقولُ» and the clause is the khabar of «كان», whose ism is the pronoun of the affair, latent in it. This was discussed at His saying: {مَا كَانَ يَصْنَعُ فِرْعَوْنُ وَقَوْمُهُ}. As for His saying «شَطَطاً», something like it was discussed in al-Kahf.

semin-durr:5-5.t: His saying: {ظَنَنَّآ أَن لَّن}: It is the lightened «أنْ», its ism is implied, and the negated clause is its khabar (predicate); the separator here is the particle of negation. «كَذِباً» is a direct object, or an adjective of an omitted maṣdar. al-Ḥasan, al-Jaḥdarī, Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and Yaʿqūb read «تَقَوَّلَ» with fatḥa on the qāf and a doubled wāw, which is the imperfect of «تَقوَّلَ», that is, "he lied." The original is «تتَقَوَّل», one of the two tāʾs having been dropped, like {تَذَكَّرُونَ} [al-Anʿām: 152]. «كَذِباً» is accusative in this reading as maṣdar, because التقوُّل is a lie, like their saying «قعدْتُ جُلوساً».

semin-durr:6-6.t: His saying: {مِّنَ الإنس}: an adjective of «رجال»; likewise His saying «من الجنِّ».

semin-durr:7-7.t: His saying: {أَن لَّن يَبْعَثَ}: like His saying: {أَن لَّن تَقُولَ} [al-Jinn: 5]. «أَنْ» and what is within its scope stand in the place of the two objects of "thinking" (ẓann). The question belongs to the chapter of iʿmāl (the competition of two governing words for one governed), because «ظنُّوا» requires two objects, and «ظَنَنْتُم» likewise; it is the working of the second, because of omission from the first. The pronoun in «أنهم ظَنُّوا» refers to humankind and that in «ظَنَنْتُم» to the jinn; the reverse is also possible, and both have been said.

semin-durr:8-8.t:
His saying: {فَوَجَدْنَاهَا}: It has two views. The more apparent is that it takes one object, because its meaning is "we met" and "we came upon"; on this view the clause «مُلِئَتْ» is in the position of the accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial). The second is that it takes two objects, so the clause is in the position of the second object.
«وحَرَساً» is accusative as tamyīz (specification), like «امتلأ الإِناءُ ماءً». الحَرَس is a collective noun for حارِس, like خَدَم for خادِم and غَيَب for غائِب, and it takes a broken plural أحْراس, as in the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:
4348 - تجاوَزْتُ أَحْراساً وأهوالَ مَعْشَرٍ ... عليَّ حِراصٍ لو يُشِرُّون مَقْتلي
(I passed guards and the terrors of a company, eager against me, who would gladly proclaim my killing.) الحارس is the guardian, the watcher, and the maṣdar is الحِراسة. «شديداً» is an adjective of «حَرَس» according to the form, as in his saying:
4349 - أخشى رُجَيْلاً ورُكَيْباً عادِياً ...
(I fear a little man on foot and a little band of riders attacking…) Had it followed the meaning, it would have been said «شِداداً» in the plural.
His saying: {وَشُهُباً}: the plural of شِهاب, like كُتُب from كِتاب. Is what is meant the stars or the guards themselves? Some of the adjectives are conjoined to others only when the wording differs, as in his saying:
4350 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . . أتى مِنْ دُونِها النَّأْيُ والبُعْدُ
(…there came between her and me distance and remoteness.) al-Aʿraj read «مُلِيَتْ» with a clear yāʾ and no hamza. مقاعِد is the plural of مَقْعَد, a noun of place.

semin-durr:9-9.t:
His saying: {الآن}: It is a present-time adverbial. It is borrowed here for the future, as in his saying:
4351 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ولكنْ ... سأسْعى الآن إذ بلغَتْ أناها
(…but I shall strive now, since its time has arrived.) So it is joined to the particle of postponement (the sīn), and this was discussed in al-Baqara at His saying {فالآن بَاشِرُوهُنَّ} [al-Baqara: 187]. «رَصَداً» is either an object of purpose (mafʿūl lahu) or an adjective of «شِهاباً», that is, "possessing a watch". al-Zamakhsharī made الرَّصَد a collective noun for الراصِد, like حَرَس, saying: "الرَّصَد is a collective noun for the watcher, like حَرَس, in the sense: possessors of a flame, watching in order to stone, and they are the angels. It may also be an adjective of الشِّهاب, in the sense of the watcher, or as in his saying:
4352 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
ومِعَىً جِياعاً
(…and hungry bowels.)" [Translator's note: the entry ends here in the source, apparently cut off mid-quotation; translated as written.]

semin-durr:10-10.t: His saying: {أَشَرٌّ أُرِيدَ}: Two views are permitted. The better is nominative by an implied verb, on the basis of preoccupation (ishtighāl); it is better because what calls for a verb precedes it, namely the interrogative particle. The second: nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject). Someone may say that the nominative by an implied verb is required here on another ground: that a verb has been conjoined with «أم», so if we imply the verb as the governor of the nominative we have conjoined a verbal clause to its like, unlike its being nominative as a mubtadaʾ, for then it takes «أم» out of being a conjunction and makes it disconnected (munqaṭiʿa), except by a remote interpretation: that the original is "Is evil intended for them or good?", so that He put His saying {أَمْ أَرَادَ بِهِمْ} in the place of "good". His saying «أشرٌ» stands in the place of the two objects of «ندري», in the sense that «ندري» is suspended (muʿallaq); and He took into account the meaning of «مَنْ» in His saying {بِهِمْ رَبُّهُمْ}, so He used the plural.

semin-durr:11-11.t:
His saying: {وَمِنَّا دُونَ ذَلِكَ}: It has two views. One: that «دونَ» means «غير», that is: "and among us are others than the righteous," and it is a mubtadaʾ (subject); it takes fatḥa only because of its annexation to something not firmly established, as in {لَقَد تَّقَطَّعَ بَيْنَكُمْ} [al-Anʿām: 94] for those who read it in the accusative, according to one of the views; al-Akhfash leaned this way. The second: that «دونَ» is in its proper adverbial sense and is an adjective of an omitted noun, the implied form being: "and among us is a group or troop short of that." The omission of the described noun with a partitive «مِنْ» is frequent, as in their saying «منا ظَعَنَ ومنَّا أقام» ("some of us departed and some of us stayed"), that is, "a group of us." The meaning: "and among us are righteous people, below those in righteousness."
His saying: {كُنَّا طَرَآئِقَ}: There are several views. First: that the implied form is "we were possessors of ways," that is, possessors of differing paths. Second: that the implied form is "we were, in the difference of our states, like different ways." Third: that the implied form is "we were in different ways," as in his saying:
4353 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... كما عَسَل الطريقَ الثَّعْلَبُ
(…as the fox runs along the road.) Fourth: that the implied form is "our ways were divided into factions," with omission of the muḍāf (first term), which is "ways", and the pronoun that was annexed to it put in its place. This was said by al-Zamakhsharī; he thus posited an omitted muḍāf in three views, since he implied in the first "possessors of", in the second "like", and in the third "our ways". The Shaykh rejected his saying "we were in ways" like the verse
. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... كما عَسَلَ الطريقَ الثعلبُ
by saying that this is not permitted except in necessity or rarity, so the Qur'an is not to be explained by it, meaning the verb becoming transitive by itself to a specific adverb of place.
القِدَد is the plural of قِدَّة, and what is meant by it is the path; its origin is conduct. One says «قِدَّةُ فلانٍ حسنةٌ», that is, his conduct is good, and it comes from «قَدَّ السَّيْرَ», that is, he cut it evenly; so it is borrowed for upright conduct. He said:
4354 - القابِضُ الباسِطُ الهادِيْ بطاعتِه ... في فِتْنة الناسِ إذا أهواؤُهم قِدَدُ
(The Withholder, the Expander, the Guide through obedience to Him, in the trial of people when their desires are divided.) And another said:
4355 - جَمَعْتَ بالرأيِ مِنهم كلَّ رافضةٍ ... إذ هم طرائقُ في أهوائِهم قِدَدُ
(By your judgment you gathered every rejecting faction of them, when they were paths, each divided in its desires.)

semin-durr:12-12.t: His saying: {فِي الأرض}: a ḥāl (circumstantial); likewise «هَرَباً», a maṣdar in the position of ḥāl. The implied form: "we shall never frustrate Him, being on the earth wherever we are in it, and we shall never frustrate Him by fleeing from it to the sky."

semin-durr:13-13.t:
His saying: {فَلاَ يَخَافُ}: that is, "so he does not fear," that is, "so he is not afraid"; and because the speech is in the implied form of a mubtadaʾ and khabar, the fāʾ has entered; had it not been so, it would have been said «لا يَخَفْ». This was said by al-Zamakhsharī, who then said: "If you ask: what is the benefit of making the verb nominative and implying a mubtadaʾ before it so that it falls as a khabar for it, and of the obligatory entry of the fāʾ, when all that could be dispensed with by saying «لا يَخَفْ»? I say: the benefit is that when he does that, it is as though it were said «فهو لا يَخافُ», which indicates the certainty that the believer is saved without doubt and that he is the one singled out for that, to the exclusion of others." I say: the reason for that is that the clause is then nominal, and the nominal clause indicates certainty and permanence more than the verbal. Ibn Wathāb and al-Aʿmash read «فلا يَخَفْ» in the jussive, and it has two views. One, and al-Zamakhsharī mentioned only this, is that «لا» is prohibitive, and the fāʾ is then obligatory. The second: that it is negating, and the fāʾ is then redundant, which is weak.
His saying: {بَخْساً}: there is an omitted muḍāf in it, that is, "recompense of deprivation" (جزاءُ بَخْسٍ); thus al-Zamakhsharī implied it, though it can be dispensed with. Ibn Wathāb read «بَخَساً» with fatḥa on the khāʾ.

semin-durr:14-14.t:
His saying: {القاسطون}: It was mentioned at the beginning of al-Nisāʾ that the triliteral «قَسَط» means "he was unjust", and the quadriliteral «أَقْسَط» means "he was just"; and that al-Ḥajjāj said to Saʿīd ibn Jubayr: "What do you say about me?" He said: "You are a qāsiṭ and ʿādil." Those present said: "How well he spoke!" He said: "O ignorant ones, he made me unjust and an unbeliever," and recited {وَأَمَّا القاسطون فَكَانُواْ لِجَهَنَّمَ حَطَباً} [al-Jinn: 15] and {ثْمَّ الذين كَفَرُواْ بِرَبِّهِمْ يَعْدِلُونَ} [al-Anʿām: 1].
His saying: {تَحَرَّوْاْ رَشَداً}: that is, they aimed at that and sought it with effort; hence التحرِّي in a matter. al-Rāghib said: "«حَرَى الشيءَ يَحْريه» means he aimed at its ḥarā, that is, its side, and «تَحَرَّاه» likewise; and «حَرَى الشيءُ يَحْرِي» means it diminished, as though it clung to the ḥarā and did not extend. He said:
4356 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ...
والمَرْءُ بعد تَمامِه يَحْرِي
(…and man, after his completion, diminishes.) One says «رَماه الله بأفعى حارِيةٍ», that is, a [diminutive] intense viper." End of quotation. Its origin seems to be from their saying «هو حَرٍ بكذا», that is, "he is worthy of it, fit for it." «رَشَداً» is a direct object. The majority read «رَشَداً» with two fatḥas; al-Aʿraj with ḍamma and sukūn.

semin-durr:16-16.t:
His saying: {وَأَلَّوِ استقاموا}: «أنْ» is the lightened one. It was mentioned in Sūrat Sabaʾ that «لو» suffices as a separator between the lightened «أَنْ» and its khabar (predicate) when the latter is a verbal clause. Abū al-Baqāʾ said here: "«لو» is a compensation, like the sīn and sawfa." It was said: «لو» means «إنْ» and «أنْ» means the lām, and that is not obligatory, as in His saying: {لَئِن لَّمْ تَنتَهِ} [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 16], while He said in another place: {وَإِن لَّمْ يَنتَهُواْ} [al-Māʾida: 73]. Ibn Faḍḍāl mentioned this in "al-Burhān." I say: this is anomalous and not to be heeded at all, because it is contrary to the grammarians. The majority read the wāw of «لو» with kasra, as originally. Ibn Wathāb and al-Aʿmash read it with ḍamma, likening it to the wāw of the pronoun; its investigation was given in al-Baqara.
His saying: {غَدَقاً}: الغَدَق with fatḥa or kasra on the dāl: two dialectal forms for abundant water, and from it الغَيْداق means abundant water, and a man who runs much or speaks much. One says «غَدِقَتْ عينُه تَغْدَقُ», that is, its tears poured abundantly. The majority read «غَدقاً» with two fatḥas. ʿĀṣim, in what al-Aʿshā transmitted from him, read it with fatḥa on the ghayn and kasra on the dāl, and it was mentioned that they are two dialectal forms.

semin-durr:17-17.t:
His saying: {يَسْلُكْهُ}: The Kufans [Translator's note: i.e. the Kufan readers] read it with the yāʾ of the third person, which is clear, since the pronoun returns to the Lord, the Exalted. The rest of the Seven read it with the nūn of majesty, by way of shifting of person (iltifāt); this is as discussed before in His saying: {سُبْحَانَ الذي أسرى} [al-Isrāʾ: 1], then He said: {بَارَكْنَا حَوْلَهُ لِنُرِيَهُ مِنْ آيَاتِنَآ}. Ibn Jundab read «نُسْلِكْه» with a nūn with ḍamma, from «أَسْلَكه». Some read it with a yāʾ (two dots below) with ḍamma, and they are two dialectal forms. One says «سَلَكه» and «أسلكه». It was recited:
3457 - حتى إذا أَسْلكوهم في قُتائِدَةٍ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Until, when they had driven them into a narrow pass…) [Translator's note: the verse number is printed as 3457 in the source, which breaks the sequence of this passage (4356, 4358); translated as written.] «سَلَكَ» and «أَسْلك» may both include the meaning of "causing to enter", and so they are transitive to two objects. It may also be said that they are transitive to one of the two objects by removal of the preposition, as in {واختار موسى قَوْمَهُ} [al-Aʿrāf: 155]. The meaning: "He will make him enter a punishment" or "He will lead him into a punishment." This holds if we say that «صَعَداً» is a maṣdar. al-Zamakhsharī said: "One says «صَعِدَ صَعَداً وصُعوداً», so the punishment is described by it, because it ascends over the one punished, that is, it rises above him and overpowers him, so he cannot bear it. From this is the saying of ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him: «ما تَصَعَّدني شيءٌ ما تَصَعَّدَتْني خطبةُ النكاحِ», meaning: nothing was harder on me, nor overcame me, as the marriage address did." As for when we make it the name of a rock in Hell, as Ibn ʿAbbās and others said, it has two views. One: that «صَعَداً» is a direct object, that is, "He will lead him in this place," and «عذاباً» is an object of purpose (mafʿūl min ajlihi). The other: that «عذاباً» is a second object, as above, and «صَعَداً» is a badal (substitute) for «عذاب», but with an omitted muḍāf (first term), that is, "the punishment of Ṣaʿad."
«صَعَداً» with two fatḥas is the reading of the majority. Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḥasan read it with ḍamma on the ṣād and fatḥa on the ʿayn; it is an adjective requiring intensification, like حُطَمٍ and لُبَدٍ. It was also read with two ḍammas, which is also an adjective, like جُنُب and شُلُل.

semin-durr:18-18.t: His saying: {وَأَنَّ المساجد}: It was mentioned that the Seven agreed on the fatḥa, and that it has two views: omission of the preposition, attached to His saying «فلا تَدْعُوا»; this is the view of al-Khalīl, who made it like His saying: {لإِيلاَفِ قُرَيْشٍ} [Quraysh: 1], which is attached to His saying {فَلْيَعْبُدُواْ} [Quraysh: 2], and like His saying: {وَإِنَّ هذه أُمَّتُكُمْ} [al-Muʾminūn: 52], that is, "and because". The second: that it is conjoined to «أنَّه استمع», so it is also revealed. Ibn Hurmuz and Ṭalḥa read «وإنَّ المساجدَ» with kasra, which admits being a fresh sentence or a causal one, in which case it is in meaning like al-Khalīl's implied form. As for المساجد, it was said that it is the plural of «مَسْجِد» with kasra, which is the place of prostration, and it was mentioned that its regular form is with fatḥa. It was also said that it is the plural of «مَسْجَد» with fatḥa, what is meant by it being the limbs mentioned in the ḥadīth: "the forehead, the nose, the two knees, the two hands and the two feet." It was also said: rather it is the plural of «مَسْجَد», a maṣdar meaning prostration, the plural being for the variety of kinds.

semin-durr:19-19.t:
His saying: {يَدْعُوهُ}: in the position of ḥāl (circumstantial), that is, "calling upon Him," that is, affirming His oneness.
His saying: {لِبَداً}: Hishām read it with ḍamma on the lām, and the rest with kasra. The first is the plural of «لُبْدَة» with ḍamma on the lām, like غُرْفة and غُرَف. It was said: rather it is a singular noun, one of the adjectives, like «حُطَم», and on this is His saying, the Exalted: {مَالاً لُّبَداً} [al-Balad: 6]. As for the second, it is the plural of «لِبْدَة» with kasra, like قِرْبَة and قِرَب. اللِّبْدَة and اللُّبْدة mean what is matted, that is, piled one part upon another; from this is the mane of the lion (لِبْدَة الأسد), as in his saying:
4358 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... له لِبْدَةٌ أظفارُه لم تُقَلَّم
(…he has a mane, and his claws have not been trimmed.) And from it comes «اللِّبْد» (felt), because of the matting of part over part. لُبَد is the name of the vulture of Luqmān ibn ʿĀd, who lived two hundred years, until they said: «طال الأمَدُ على لُبَدٍ» ("the term has grown long for Lubad"). The meaning: the jinn were almost upon him in piled-up groups, crowded upon him like felt.
al-Ḥasan and al-Jaḥdarī read «لُبُداً» with two ḍammas, and a group transmitted it from Abū ʿAmr; it admits two views. One: that it is the plural of «لَبْد», like «رُهُن», the plural of «رَهْن». The other: that it is the plural of «لَبُود», like صَبور and صُبُر, which is also a form of intensification. Ibn Muḥayṣin read it with ḍamma and sukūn; this may be a lightening of the reading before it, or it may be an adjective in its own right. al-Ḥasan and al-Jaḥdarī also read «لُبَّداً» with ḍamma on the lām and shadda on the bāʾ, the plural of «لابِد», like ساجِد and سُجَّد, راكع and رُكَّع. Abū Rajāʾ read it with kasra on the lām and shadda on the bāʾ, which is very unusual.

semin-durr:20-20.t: His saying: {قُلْ إِنَّمَآ أَدْعُو}: ʿĀṣim and Ḥamza read «قُلْ» in the form of the imperative, by way of shifting of person, that is: "Say, O Muḥammad." The rest read «قال» as a report about the servant of Allah, who is Muḥammad ﷺ. al-Jaḥdarī said: "It is so in the codex." Parallels to that were given before in {قُلْ سُبْحَانَ رَبِّي} [al-Isrāʾ: 93] at the end of al-Isrāʾ, and likewise at the beginning of al-Anbiyāʾ [verse 4] and at the end of al-Muʾminūn.

semin-durr:21-21.t: His saying: {ضَرّاً وَلاَ رَشَداً}: al-Aʿraj read «رُشُداً» with two ḍammas. He made الضَّرّ an expression for error (الغَيّ), because harm is a consequence and a fruit of error, so he put the effect in place of its cause. The original: "I do not possess error or right guidance," so he mentioned the more important. It was also said: rather, there are two omissions in the speech, and the original is: "I do not possess for you harm or benefit, or error or right guidance," so from each one he omitted what its counterpart indicates.

semin-durr:22-22.t:
His saying: {مُلْتَحَداً}: the object of «أَجِدُ», because it means "I meet" and "I find". المُلْتَحَد here means the course and the way. He said:
4359 - يا لَهْفَ نفسي ولَهْفي غيرُ مُجْديَةٍ ... عَنِّي وما مِنْ قضاءِ الله مُلْتَحَدُ
(Alas for my soul, and my alas is of no avail to me; and there is no refuge from the decree of Allah.) that is, an escape and a way.

semin-durr:23-23.t:
His saying: {إِلاَّ بَلاَغاً}: There are several views. First: that it is a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ), that is: "but if I convey from Allah, He will have mercy on me," because conveyance from Allah does not fall under His saying {وَلَنْ أَجِدَ مِن دُونِهِ مُلْتَحَداً}, since it is not from other than Allah; rather it is from Allah, and by His help and granting of success. Second: that it is connected. Its interpretation: protection is borrowed for conveyance, since it is its cause and the cause of His mercy, the Exalted; the meaning: "I shall find no cause to which I may incline and by which I may hold fast, except that I convey and obey, so that He protects me." When it is connected, its accusative is permissible in two ways. One, which is the more preferable, is that it is a badal (substitute) for «مُلْتحداً», because the speech is not affirmative. The other: that it is accusative as an exception; Abū Isḥāq held the view of substitution. Third: that it is excepted from His saying: {لاَ أَمْلِكُ لَكُمْ ضَرّاً}. Qatāda said: "that is, I have no power for you except conveyance to you."
al-Zamakhsharī set it out and said: "that is, I have no power except conveyance from Allah, and {قُلْ إِنِّي لَن يُجِيرَنِي} is a parenthetical clause inserted to confirm the denial of capacity." The Shaykh said: "There is remoteness in it because of the length of separation between them." I say: where is the length, when separation by more than this has occurred? On this view the exception is disconnected. Fourth: that the sentence is not an exception but a condition. The original is «إنْ لا», which was assimilated; so «إنْ» is conditional, its verb is omitted because its maṣdar and the first sentence indicate it, and «لا» is negating; the implied form: "If I do not convey a conveyance from Allah, then no one will protect me from Him." They made this like the saying of the poet:
4360 - فطَلِّقْها فَلَسْتَ لها بكُفْءٍ ... وإلاَّ يَعْلُ مَفْرِقَكَ الحُسامُ
(Divorce her, for you are not her equal; otherwise the sword will rise over your head-parting.) that is, "and if you do not divorce her, it will rise," omitting the condition and keeping the answer. This view is weak for two reasons. One: that omission of the condition without its particle is very rare. The other: that both parts were omitted together, I mean the condition and the answer, so it would be like his saying:
4361 - قالَتْ بناتُ العَمِّ يا سَلْمى وإنْ ... كان فقيراً مُعْدَماً قالت: وإِنْ
(The cousins said, "O Salmā, even if he is poor and destitute," she said: "Even if.") that is, she said: "Even if he is poor, I am pleased with him." It may be said: the answer is either present according to those who permit its being put first, or has the force of what is pronounced, since what precedes it indicates it.
His saying: {مِّنَ الله}: It has two views. One: that «مِنْ» means «عَنْ», because «بَلِّغ» is made transitive with it, and from it is his saying, peace be upon him: «ألا بَلِّغوا عني» ("Convey from me"). The other: that it is attached to an omitted element as an adjective of «بلاغ». al-Zamakhsharī said: "«مِن» is not a ṣila (complement) of the conveying; it is in the position of «مِنْ» in His saying {بَرَآءَةٌ مِّنَ الله} [al-Tawba: 1], meaning: a conveyance coming from Allah."
His saying: {وَرِسَالاَتِهِ}: There are two views. One: that it is accusative, a conjunction on «بلاغاً», as though it were said: "I have no power for you except the conveyance and the messages"; al-Zamakhsharī mentioned only this. The other: that it is genitive, conjoined to the Majestic Name, that is: "except a conveyance from Allah and from His messages"; thus the Shaykh implied it, and he made it the apparent view. He took liberty in making «مِنْ» mean «عن», and liberty with particles is a Kufan view, and even so it is not regular according to them.
His saying: {فَإِنَّ لَهُ نَارَ}: The majority read «إنَّ» with kasra, making it an independent clause after the fāʾ of the apodosis. Ṭalḥa read it with fatḥa, as it, with what is within its scope, is interpreted as a maṣdar standing as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, the implied form being: "his recompense is that he has the fire of Gehenna" or "his ruling is that he has the fire of Gehenna." Ibn Khālawayh said: "I heard Ibn Mujāhid say: no one read it so, and it is a grammatical error, because it comes after the fāʾ of the condition." He said: "And I heard Ibn al-Anbārī say: it is correct, and its meaning is 'his recompense is that he has the fire of Gehenna.'" I say: Ibn Mujāhid, although an imam in the readings, did not see its explanation, and this is very strange. How did he overlook the two readings of {فَأنَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَّحِيمٌ} in al-Anʿām [verse 54]? No wonder Ibn al-Anbārī approved the reading, given his wide range in Arabic.
His saying: {خَالِدِينَ}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ in «له», and the governing word is the settling to which this preposition and its genitive noun are attached; it is carried over to the meaning of «مَنْ», and that is why it is in the plural.

semin-durr:24-24.t:
His saying: {حتى إِذَا}: al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: to what is «حتى» attached, such that what follows it is made its goal? I say: to His saying {يَكُونُونَ عَلَيْهِ لِبَداً} [al-Jinn: 19], in that they support one another against him in enmity, regard his helpers as weak, and regard his numbers as few, until, when they see what they are promised, whether from the day of Badr and Allah's giving him victory over them, or from the Day of Resurrection, they will then know who is weaker in helper." He said: "It is also possible that it is attached to an omitted element which the circumstance indicates, namely the unbelievers' regarding as weak and as few his numbers, as though he said: they will not cease to be as they are until, when they see what they are promised, the polytheists said: 'When is this promise?' in denial of it, and he said: 'Say: it will surely come to pass, without doubt.'" The Shaykh said: "His saying 'to what is it attached?': if he means the attachment of a preposition, it is not correct, because it is a particle of commencement and what follows it is not in the position of the genitive, contrary to al-Zajjāj and Ibn Durustawayh, who claimed that when it is a particle of commencement, the initial clause after it is in the position of the genitive. If he means by attachment the connection of what follows it to what precedes it, and that what follows it is the goal of what precedes it, then it is correct. As for his implying that it is attached to His saying {يَكُونُونَ عَلَيْهِ لِبَداً}, that is very remote because of the length of separation between them by many clauses. Some implied that omitted element to which the goal applies, saying: the implied form is 'leave them until when…'. al-Tabrīzī said: 'It may be a goal for an omitted element,' without making clear what it is. The Shaykh said: 'What appears is that it is a goal of what the preceding clause contains, namely the ruling that the Fire is theirs. It is as though it were said: the disobedient is judged to have the Fire, and the ruling of that is a threat, until when they see what has been ruled to be theirs, they will know.'"
His saying: {مَنْ أَضْعَفُ}: «مَنْ» may be interrogative, so it is nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and «أضعفُ» is its khabar (predicate); the clause is in the position of the accusative, standing in the place of the two objects, because it is suspending (muʿallaq) the "knowing" before it. Or it may be a relative noun (mawṣūl), and «أَضْعَفُ» is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is, "he is weakest"; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) and the returning pronoun. The omission is made fair by the length of the ṣila through the tamyīz (specification). The relative noun is an object of "knowing" in the sense of "being acquainted with".

semin-durr:25-25.t: His saying: {أَقَرِيبٌ}: a khabar (predicate) put first, and «ما تُوعَدون» is the [mubtadaʾ (subject)]. It is also possible that «قريبٌ» is the mubtadaʾ, relying on the interrogative, and «ما تُوعَدون» is its agent, that is, "is what you are promised near?", like «أقائمٌ أبواك». «ما» may be relative, so the returning pronoun is omitted, or maṣdar-forming, so there is no returning pronoun. «أم» is apparently connected (muttaṣila). al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: what is the meaning of {أَمْ يَجْعَلُ لَهُ ربي أَمَداً}, when the term may be near or far? Do you not see His saying {تَوَدُّ لَوْ أَنَّ بَيْنَهَا وَبَيْنَهُ أَمَدَاً بَعِيداً} [Āl ʿImrān: 30]? I say: the Prophet ﷺ regarded the promise as near, so it is as though he said: 'I do not know whether it is a state expected at every hour or a postponed one for which a limit has been set.'"

semin-durr:26-26.t:
His saying: {عَالِمُ الغيب}: The majority read it in the nominative: either as a badal (substitute) for «ربي», or as a clarification of it, or as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is, "He is the Knower." It was also read in the accusative, as praise (madḥ). al-Suddī read «عَلِمَ الغيبَ», a past verb governing «الغيب» in the accusative.
His saying: {فَلاَ يُظْهِرُ}: The majority read it from «أظْهر», and «أحَداً» is a direct object. al-Ḥasan read «يَظْهَرُ» with fatḥa on the yāʾ and the hāʾ, from the triliteral «ظَهَر»; «أحَدٌ» is its agent.

semin-durr:27-27.t:
His saying: {إِلاَّ مَنِ ارتضى}: It may be disconnected (munqaṭiʿ), that is: "but whomever He approves, He makes him aware of what He wills of His unseen by revelation." His saying «مِنْ رسولٍ» is a clarification of those who are approved.
His saying: {فَإِنَّهُ يَسْلُكُ}: a clarification of that. It was also said that it is connected. As for «رَصَداً», it has already been discussed. «مَنْ» may be conditional, or a relative noun including the meaning of a condition. His saying «فإنَّه» is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ on both views. It is also a disconnected exception, that is, "but". The meaning: "but whomever He approves of the messengers, He assigns to him angels as watchers who guard him."

semin-durr:28-28.t:
His saying: {لِّيَعْلَمَ}: attached to «يَسْلُكُ». The majority read it in the active, and there is disagreement about it, that is: "that Muḥammad ﷺ may know." It was said: "that he may know," that is, "that his knowledge may become apparent to people." It was said: "that Iblīs may know." It was said: "that the polytheists may know." It was said: "that the angels may know"; these last two are weak because of the singular pronoun. The pronoun in «أَبْلَغُوا» returns to «مَنْ» in «مَنْ ارتَضَى»: first he took into account its form, so he used the singular in His saying {مِن بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِ}, and then its meaning, so he used the plural in «أَبْلَغُوا» and so on.
Ibn ʿAbbās and Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «لِيُعْلَمَ» in the passive. Ibn Abī ʿAbla and al-Zuhrī read «لِيُعْلِمَ» with ḍamma on the yāʾ and kasra on the lām, that is: "that Allah and His Messenger may make known by that." Abū Ḥaywa read «رسالة» in the singular, though the plural is meant. Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «وأُحِيْط وأُحْصِيَ» in the passive, with «كلُّ» nominative as the subject of «أُحْصِي».
His saying: {عَدَداً}: It may be a tamyīz (specification) transferred from the direct object. The original: "He counted the number of everything," as in His saying, the Exalted: {وَفَجَّرْنَا الأرض عُيُوناً} [al-Qamar: 12], that is, "the springs of the earth," according to a disagreement mentioned earlier. It may also be accusative as maṣdar in sense, because «أحصَى» means "counted", so it is as though it were said: "and counted everything," the verb tending to the maṣdar. Makkī denied that it is a maṣdar, because of the clear (non-assimilated) form, saying: "«عَدَداً» is accusative as clarification, and if it were a maṣdar it would have been assimilated." I say: he means that its regular form would be on the pattern فَعْل with sukūn on the ʿayn, but that is not obligatory, so its maṣdar came with fatḥa on the ʿayn. Since «لِيَعْلَمَ» includes the meaning "he has known that", the conjunction of «وأحاط» to that implied element is permitted.
